CONSISTENCY RECORD: this chapter asks what silicones are three times — at two marks here, at four marks with the preparation added, and at eight marks with the preparation, a worked example and the uses added. All three state the same chemistry: synthetic organosilicon polymers, repeating unit R₂SiO, neighbouring silicon atoms joined through oxygen as Si–O–Si, R an alkyl or an aryl group. The water repelling property is stated on this card and on the eight-mark card, and is deliberately not on the four-mark preparation card, which stops at the definition and the three-step route. The longer cards carry ADDITIONAL content rather than the same content at greater length; this two-mark card stops at the definition and the Si–O–Si chain and prints no preparation and no uses.

insider_note: Two things make this answer complete: the words organosilicon polymer, and the repeating unit R₂SiO written down as a formula. A description of silicon and oxygen with no R₂SiO on the page has not said what a silicone is.

steps.why: A silicone is named by its repeating unit, not by a list of the elements in it. Writing R₂SiO fixes the two facts that separate a silicone from every other silicon compound: one oxygen atom and two organic groups on each silicon atom.
common_mistakes: Calling a silicone a silicate. A silicate carries no organic group on the silicon; a silicone carries two.
Writing the repeating unit as SiO₂. That is silica. The repeating unit of a silicone is R₂SiO.
steps.memory_tip: Read R₂SiO as two organic groups and one oxygen atom on every silicon atom.
steps.margin_note: Write the repeating unit R₂SiO on its own line. The words organosilicon polymer alone do not show it.

lines.text: The chain is a run of Si–O–Si linkages

steps.why: The oxygen atoms are inside the chain and the organic groups are outside it. That one arrangement explains both halves of the name: the silicon and oxygen chain is the silicon part, and the outward organic groups are the organo part.
common_mistakes: Joining the silicon atoms to each other directly. Neighbouring silicon atoms are joined through an oxygen atom, as Si–O–Si.
Leaving the R groups off the silicon atoms. Without them the chain is silica, not a silicone.
steps.memory_tip: Oxygen inside the chain, organic groups outside it.
steps.margin_note: One closing line naming the Si–O–Si linkage completes the answer.
